job.title: WHS Advisor
job.description:
Who’s hiring?
CMV Group, a true South Australian icon and one of South Australia's largest privately owned businesses, is looking for an experienced WHS Advisor to join its growing team.

With more than 90 years of business success, CMV employs approximately 2,000 people across South Australia and Victoria and operates some of the most progressive franchises within the automotive and agricultural industries.
What really stands out about this opportunity is the importance placed on safety across the Group. Safety First is CMV’s number one value – it’s embedded in the way the business operates and the work of the WHS team is highly regarded across the organisation.

It’s also an exciting time to join. The WHS function is growing and continuing to evolve, creating an opportunity to not only step into an established environment with good systems and frameworks already in place, but to contribute ideas, get involved in projects and help shape how the function develops from here.

So, what’s the role?
Based from CMV Group’s Greenhill Road office, this is a hands-on WHS Advisor position supporting businesses and sites predominantly across metropolitan Adelaide, with occasional travel to regional South Australian locations.

You’ll work closely with managers and leaders across the Group, providing practical WHS advice, coaching and guidance while building their capability and driving continuous improvement in safety practices.

This isn’t a role where you’ll spend your week sitting behind a desk. You’ll be visible across the business, building relationships, understanding how different sites operate and working alongside leaders to identify opportunities and achieve better safety outcomes.

There’s plenty of variety, autonomy and scope to make an impact. You’ll have established systems and frameworks to work with, the support of a WHS Coordinator and the opportunity to be involved in broader WHS projects as the function continues to grow and evolve.

A typical week might see you:
  • Building strong relationships across sites and influencing positive safety behaviours
  • Identifying hazards, assessing risks and working with leaders to implement practical controls
  • Leading incident investigations and ensuring actions and outcomes are followed through
  • Conducting internal WHS audits and contributing to external audits
  • Supporting the ongoing implementation and improvement of WHS systems, policies and procedures
  • Keeping leaders informed of relevant legislative changes and WHS requirements
  • Identifying training needs and facilitating WHS training where required
  • Contributing to monthly safety reporting, research and broader WHS projects
  • Helping drive a proactive, positive safety culture across the Group.
Who are you?
You’re an experienced WHS professional who is passionate about making workplaces safer and enjoys being out in the business, partnering with people rather than simply policing process.

You’ll need a level of confidence in this role. You’ll be working with managers and leaders across a diverse group of businesses, so you need to be comfortable holding your own, providing advice and constructively challenging when required. Just as importantly, you know that influencing better safety outcomes starts with relationships – you’re approachable, credible and able to bring people with you.

You’re proactive and motivated, with a genuine interest in improving WHS across an organisation. You notice the detail, follow things through and don’t wait for an issue to arise before looking for ways things could be done better.

You’ll bring:
  • Previous experience in a WHS Advisor or similar role, ideally with a Certificate IV in WHS/OHS
  • Sound knowledge of WHS legislation, standards and regulations
  • Confident communicator with strong relationship-building and stakeholder influencing skills
  • Proactive, organised and detail-focused, with the ability to drive improvements and follow actions through
  • A current driver’s licence and willingness to travel between sites.
Experience within workshop, automotive, agricultural or similarly operational environments would be advantageous, but isn’t essential.

What’s in it for you?
  • Some flexibility to work from home on an ad-hoc basis
  • Ongoing development and career growth within a large and progressive organisation
  • Access to a range of benefits including health and wellbeing programs, insurance offers and a paid volunteering program
  • Car allowance and fully reimbursed travel expenses
  • Australian Health and Safety Institute (AIHS) membership
  • Corporate discounts on income and health insurance programs
  • Paid volunteering and study support opportunities
  • Annual staff dinners, Christmas picnics and other wellbeing activities

How to apply
To apply, send your cover letter and resume by clicking APPLY below and we’ll handle the rest!

For a confidential discussion, contact Melanie at Mansfield & Co on 0411 471 822.

job.title: Expression of Interest for Temporary Opportunities
job.description:
Expression of Interest | Temporary & Contract Opportunities

Please note: This is an Expression of Interest advertisement and is not for a specific current vacancy.

At Mansfield & Co, we regularly partner with organisations across Adelaide looking for talented people to step into temporary and contract roles – from short-term assignments of a couple of weeks through to longer-term contracts of up to 12 months. Opportunities can be part-time or full-time, depending on the needs of each organisation.

We work with a diverse range of organisations across Adelaide, from small and medium-sized businesses through to larger organisations, not-for-profits and community-based organisations. Our clients span industries including professional services, health and community services, education, energy, manufacturing and more.

We’re looking to grow our network of candidates who are open to temporary or contract work, so when the right opportunity comes up, we know who to call!

We’d love to hear from people with experience across:
  • Human Resources – HR Administration, HR Coordination, HR Advisory, HR Business Partnering and senior HR/generalist roles
  • Finance & Payroll – Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Payroll, Assistant Accounting, Accounting, Financial/Management Accounting and Finance Management
  • Administration & Office Support – Reception, Administration, Executive/Personal Assistance, Office Management and senior administrative support
  • Customer Service & Client Support – Customer Service, Contact Centre, Membership, Client Services and Team Leadership
What kind of opportunities could come up?
Temporary and contract assignments can vary quite a bit. You might be looking for a short-term role for a few weeks, a contract spanning several months or up to 12 months or simply want the flexibility that temp and contract work can offer.

We see both part-time and full-time opportunities, with roles coming up across Adelaide, from the CBD through to the inner suburbs and further afield. Hours and working arrangements will vary depending on each assignment.

What we’d love to know about you
If you’re interested in joining our temp network, send through your CV along with an indication of:
  • The type and level of work you’re interested in
  • Your availability and when you could start
  • Whether you’re looking for part-time or full-time opportunities
  • Your preferred locations
  • Whether you’re interested in short-term, long-term or both types of assignments
Enough about us - let’s talk about whether temping could work for you!
Whether you’re immediately available, between permanent roles, returning to work, or simply prefer the flexibility of contract work, we’d love to hear from you.

Again, please note that this advertisement is for Expressions of Interest only and does not relate to a specific current vacancy. Applying will allow our team to consider you for suitable temporary and contract opportunities as they arise.

job.title: Multiple Temporary Administration & Project-Based Roles
job.description:
Multiple Temporary Administration & Project-Based Roles

We’re partnering with an established organisation looking for three professionals to join its team. We're looking for:
  • Senior Administration Coordinator
  • Project Administrator
  • Project Document Controller
All three roles will commence as 3-month full-time temporary contracts, with a strong likelihood of becoming permanent after this period.

Across all three roles, a typical week might see you:
  • Coordinating meetings, diaries, travel and general office administration
  • Preparing reports, presentations, correspondence and project documents
  • Maintaining filing systems, registers and controlled documentation
  • Supporting document workflows, approvals and version control
  • Liaising with senior leaders, project teams and external stakeholders
  • Assisting with onboarding, reporting and broader project support
Which role sounds like you?
  • Senior Administration Coordinator: Proven experience in a senior administration or office coordination role, along with exposure to document control.
  • Project Administrator: Project administration or executive support experience, with advanced PowerPoint skills. Visio experience would be highly regarded.
  • Project Document Controller: Previous document control experience within a project environment. InEight experience is preferred.
Experience working within a complex project environment will be highly regarded across all three positions.

What’s in it for you?
  • CBD location
  • Initial 3-month, full-time temporary contracts
  • Strong likelihood of becoming permanent
  • Good hourly rates
  • Join a growing team supporting a major project
How to apply
Please apply with an up-to-date CV and let us know which role or roles you would like to be considered for.

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Who's hiring?

For over 25 years, Caledonia Group has delivered scaffolding, rope access, insulation, cladding and engineering solutions across the mining, energy, infrastructure and commercial sectors in Australia, New Zealand and beyond. We support some of the biggest and most complex projects in the region, backed by uncompromising safety standards and a leadership team with deep industry experience. Just as importantly, we're a genuinely good place to work — a close, down-to-earth crew that's small enough that everyone knows everyone, where people pick up the phone rather than fire off an email, and where Friday afternoons, team lunches and the odd toolbox pizza are all part of how the place ticks. As we continue to grow, we're looking for a Financial Accountant to keep our reporting sharp and our numbers telling a clear story.

So, what's the role?

Reporting to an experienced Finance Director, you'll take ownership of month-end management and reporting across the Group. You'll work closely alongside the broader finance team, and partner with Directors and operational teams — including Claims and Contracts Administrators across SA, WA, NSW and New Zealand — to make sure the numbers land with the people who rely on them.

There's a real appetite here for someone who'll improve things rather than simply maintain them — the general ledger could do with a tidy, and there's scope to sharpen reporting, controls and systems as you go. It's an ideal role for someone with sound technical grounding who's ready to take on more than their current position allows.

Here's what a typical week might look like:
  • Owning the month-end close and preparing consolidated P&L, balance sheet and cashflow reporting
  • Producing monthly management packs with variance analysis and commentary — and the operational insight that helps teams act on them
  • Completing intercompany and balance sheet reconciliations across all entities
  • Supporting the annual budget, quarterly reforecasts and job/project profitability analysis
  • Delivering KPIs and decision-support to the Finance Director and operational leaders
  • Preparing weekly and monthly cashflow forecasts, monitoring working capital and supporting banking and financing arrangements
  • Owning compliance across the Group, including BAS, and strengthening financial controls, governance and the annual audit
  • Approving payroll and supporting the wider finance team
  • Driving process and system improvements across finance and reporting
Enough about us—let's talk about whether this role is for you!

You're someone who enjoys getting into the detail, takes pride in accurate work and likes building relationships across a business rather than staying behind the numbers. You're proactive, organised and happiest when you're improving a process, not just keeping it running.

Technically speaking, you:
  • Hold a degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline, with CA or CPA completed or underway
  • Have sound financial accounting fundamentals — month-end close, journals, accruals and reconciliations
  • Bring strong compliance skills — including BAS — along with balance sheet reconciliation experience
  • Have exposure to multi-entity reporting and consolidation, or the appetite to pick it up quickly
  • Are a confident communicator who can work with Directors and operational teams and explain the numbers to people outside finance
  • Bring the kind of operational insight that turns reporting into something teams can act on
  • Have working knowledge of payroll (an advantage)
  • Have experience with MYOB and Xero, or similar systems including Modano (an advantage)
A commercial background in a project-based or operationally driven business will be well regarded, though it isn't essential.

What's in it for you?
  • Join a $100m+ national construction business in a stable, growing sector
  • Work alongside an experienced Finance Director and respected leadership team
  • A down-to-earth team where everyone knows everyone, with flexible core hours and one day a week from home
  • A long-term, secure career path with genuine room to grow
  • Competitive salary 
How to apply?

Click that apply button — we'd love to hear from you. For a confidential discussion, contact Tracy Frankenfeld at Mansfield & Co on 0493 703 697 or tracy@mansfieldandco.com.au

job.title: Administration & Finance Officer
job.description:
Who's hiring?
Distribution 360 are a proudly South Australian business who are doing their bit to create a cleaner environment.

We work with local councils, businesses and residents to safely remove and reliably recycle rubbish across our state. We're focussed on getting the job done quickly and cleanly and offer a range of services including our end-to-end bulky goods removal and mattress recycling.

Ultimately, we're a passionate group of locals who are doing their bit to create a rubbish-responsible future for our planet.

We're on the hunt for an Administration Officer to work in a job share arrangement, keeping our office – and our drivers – organised and on track.

So, what's the role?
Your day starts with reviewing the previous day's dockets to reconcile and invoice each job.

You'll take ownership of accounts receivable and payable, including taking payments, and keeping things running smoothly by scheduling and planning the day ahead – building the skeleton structure for upcoming jobs. Email management is a big part of the role too, coordinating logistics and calls with our drivers and customers.

You'll also pull together regular reporting to keep the team informed and take care of some light housekeeping and amenities for your own workspace (we have a cleaner in routinely).

What are we looking for?
We’re looking for someone who loves organising - and keeping others organised!

You’re also someone who can be relied on to get the job done but is also up to helping the team with broader tasks when required.

You're reliable, and comfortable managing your workload without losing your attention to detail. You'll be confident with AR/AP, reconciliations and invoicing, and a whiz with technology including Outlook and Excel.  Cash Flow Manager experience would be an advantage but is not essential.

You’ll love engaging with our customers and ensuring high quality support and resolution of scheduling requirements.

You're happy working closely alongside a teammate but just as comfortable holding down the fort on your own to keep things ticking along. 

What's in it for you?
We're offering this role on a part time basis – 2 to 3 days a week, with the need to pick up extra shifts covering leave. You'll typically start around 9am with the option to wrap up on-site by 3pm, then shift to a short work-from-home stretch monitoring calls and emails until 5pm.

Your regular office days can be negotiated to suit, with one work-from-home day each week – a great mix of routine and flexibility.

We're also offering a competitive hourly rate, reviewed in line with experience.
Most importantly, we are passionate about offering a workplace where our team feels valued.

How do I apply?
If you fit the brief and are excited by the opportunity to contribute to a great local business who is doing their bit for the world, we can't wait to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, contact Tracy Frankenfeld at Mansfield & Co on 0493 703 697 or tracy@mansfieldandco.com.au

job.title: Submissions Coordinator
job.description:
Who’s hiring?
FMG Engineering is an award-winning, multi-disciplinary engineering consultancy with more than 50 years' experience and a presence across South Australia, Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland.

With a team of more than 180 people nationally, FMG brings together engineers, scientists, technicians and other professionals to work across a diverse range of projects. Their culture is built around integrity, teamwork and collaboration, with people encouraged to share ideas and contribute to better outcomes.

Importantly, this is a business that genuinely values work/life balance. Flexibility is embedded in the way they work, with options including working from home, flexible hours and, after 12 months, the opportunity to work a compressed fortnight.

So, what’s the role?
Reporting to the Business Development Manager, you'll take ownership of the end-to-end coordination of FMG's submissions nationally, from smaller EOIs through to larger and more complex tenders.

This is an opportunity to bring your expertise and ideas to the role – refining what's already in place, identifying opportunities to improve and continuing to elevate the quality of FMG's submissions.

In this busy yet rewarding role you’ll:
  • Coordinate EOIs, RFPs and tender submissions from start to finish
  • Establish submission schedules, review milestones and version control
  • Work with stakeholders across the business to gather information and develop strong, compelling content
  • Draft and edit non-technical content, including company information, project experience and capability statements
  • Format and produce professional submissions using Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Adobe InDesign
  • Develop graphics including organisation charts, infographics and presentations
  • Maintain the bid knowledge library, including project sheets, CVs, imagery and corporate information
  • Support the BD Manager with tender monitoring and coordination of BD and client meetings
  • Coordinate industry awards and proposals alongside the marketing team
  • Bring ideas to continually refine and improve the submissions process
While you'll be supporting the business nationally, no travel is required.

What are we looking for?
We're looking for someone who knows the submissions space and is confident taking ownership of it.

Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Previous experience coordinating bids, tenders, proposals or submissions
  • Experience within the engineering or construction sector
  • Excellent written communication skills and a strong eye for detail
  • Strong Microsoft Word and PowerPoint skills, with Adobe Creative Suite experience highly regarded
  • The ability to work independently, prioritise competing deadlines and keep things moving
  • Confidence building relationships and working with stakeholders across different areas of the business
  • A proactive approach – you're comfortable bringing ideas forward and looking for ways to improve
  • A genuine sense of pride in the quality of work you produce
What’s in it for you?
Along with a role where you'll have plenty of ownership and the opportunity to make an impact, FMG offers:
  • Work from home up to two days per week once established
  • Flexible working hours and a genuine focus on work/life balance
  • Access to a compressed working fortnight after 12 months
  • Ability for full-time employees to purchase additional leave
  • One paid volunteer day each year
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Training and professional development support - Employee recognition and service awards
If you're an experienced Submissions Coordinator looking for more ownership, flexibility and the opportunity to bring your ideas to a business that values quality and balance, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Melanie Mansfield at Mansfield & Co Recruitment on 0411 471 822.
